## Architecture

`engage` step 3 gains an idea input. When the ask names an open `composer:idea`, or the user asks to start from an idea, `engage` reads the idea and sets focus from its effort, or routes to `init` for a new effort when the idea has none. It keeps the idea subject in the routing line. `init` step 6 and `settle-phase` step 1 each gain one write: supersede the idea to `promoted` with the refs that now exist.

## Interfaces

- Routing line: `idea: <subject> | none`.
- Read: `canon list --type composer:idea --subject <subject> --exact-subject --full`.
- Write, from `init` or `settle-phase`: `canon supersede --type composer:idea --id <id> --expected-revision <revision> --payload '{"status":"promoted","effort":"<effort-slug>","phase":"<phase-slug>"}'`.

## Decisions

- `idea-promotion-writer`: `init` and `settle-phase` write the promotion.
- Earlier: `composer-idea-lifecycle`.

## Invariants

- `engage` writes no records for the idea path.
- A promoted idea always has a valid effort ref.

## Assumptions

- `init` creates the effort before the user can abandon after it, so a promoted idea always has a live effort behind it.
- The chat keeps the idea subject between skills; the routing line is the explicit carrier.

## Tradeoffs

- Three skills change instead of one.
- The promote step sits in a skill that may not run if the user stops after `engage`; the idea then stays `open`, which is correct.

## Risks

- Skills drift if only one of the three is edited. The contract tests cover all three.
- The routing-line change touches every skill that reads it. Plan-phase lists them.
- `skills/engage/SKILL.md` is edited by phase `backlog-to-idea` too. Run the phases in order.
